overall: The AG found the Methuen City Council violated the Open Meeting Law by deliberating non-Purpose 3 budget matters in executive session and by failing to keep minutes of that session, but found no violation over the recording gap, and ordered minutes created and released.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly discussed matters in executive session that should have been held in open session, after the executive session shifted from union contract talks to an interim budget.
allegations.key_passage: Upon review, we find that the deliberations occurring after that point should have been reserved for open session.

allegations.summary: Council allegedly failed to create or maintain minutes of the June 25, 2010 executive session.
allegations.key_passage: But the City Council did not create or maintain minutes for the June 25, 2010 executive session.

allegations.summary: Recording secretary was asked to leave during executive session, allegedly creating a gap in the audio recording that violated the law.
allegations.key_passage: though the recording is inaudible at times, there is no discernible gap in it.

remedy: Create and approve the minutes of the June 25, 2010 executive session as soon as possible and no later than 10 days after receipt of the determination.
Create and make public immediately the portion of the minutes covering deliberations on subject matter outside Purpose 3, beginning at approximately when the recording secretary exited.
Review the earlier portion of the executive session minutes in due course and release them if the reason for entering executive session no longer applies.
Preserve the executive session recordings and make them available as public records, per the Municipal Records Retention Schedule, upon request.
remedy_passage: We specifically order that the Council create and make public immediately the portion of the minutes during which the Council deliberated on subject matter not appropriate for executive session under Purpose 3, beginning at approximately the time the recording secretary exited the Council chambers.
